changes.before: Signed 2026-07-14; DEC must hold in abeyance incomplete discretionary permit applications for covered data centers until DPS submits the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and findings statement.
changes.after: Signed 2026-07-14; directs the specified DEC application hold until DPS submits its report of the final GEIS and associated findings statement. Current legal effect through 2026-11-05 is unresolved.

changes.before: Binding state-agency permitting restriction for data centers that consume or can consume 50 MW or more: DEC must hold incomplete discretionary permits, approvals, licenses, and similar permissions while DPS completes a statewide Generic Environmental Impact Statement; it does not override local permitting or zoning.
changes.after: Directs DEC to hold discretionary applications for construction or expansion of covered data centers that are or become pending before DEC and were not determined complete before 2026-07-14. Coverage follows the order's complete definition, including equipment/service characteristics and the 50-MW criterion and listed exclusions, including primarily manufacturing, research, education or medical-care facilities. Local-government permissions are excluded.

changes.before: Ends when DPS submits the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and associated findings statement; the order excludes local-government permits, approvals, licenses, and similar permissions.
changes.after: The DEC application hold lasts until DPS submits its report of the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and associated findings statement. This is not a fixed twelve-month term or an endpoint for every provision of the order; cutoff-date satisfaction remains unverified.

changes.before: Governor directive issued 2026-08-03; ERCOT implementation notice issued 2026-08-03.
changes.after: Governor directive signed 2026-08-03. Current legal effect and satisfaction of its audit prerequisite through 2026-11-05 are unresolved.

changes.before: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to verify and audit every data center advancing through ERCOT interconnection before it may move forward, pausing the Batch Zero process pending the required review.
changes.after: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT interconnection before additional data centers are approved to move forward; noncompliant projects must be denied connection. Required information includes public financial assistance, power, water and cooling, community impacts, and ownership.

changes.before: Until PUCT and ERCOT complete the comprehensive verification and audit; projects that fail applicable requirements must be denied grid connection.
changes.after: Comprehensive verification and audit is required before additional interconnection approvals; the separate denial requirement applies to noncompliant projects. The letter states no fixed end date. Satisfaction of the prerequisite through 2026-11-05 is unverified.

changes.before: Sen. Phil King and Sen. Charles Schwertner; House sponsor Rep. Phil King
changes.after: Senate authors King and Schwertner; House sponsor King (given-name identities not independently verified in this review).

changes.before: Passed Senate 2025-03-19 (with amendments); passed House 2025-05-27 (RV#3643); Senate concurred in House amendments 2025-05-29; signed by Governor 2025-06-20, effective immediately.
changes.after: Certified Senate passage 2025-03-19; House passage with amendments 2025-05-27; Senate concurrence 2025-05-29. Official history records effective immediately 2025-06-20. Governor signature date and House roll-call identifier are not independently verified here.

changes.before: Requires PUCT/ERCOT large-load planning and interconnection standards; applies to large loads at a default 75 MW single-site threshold; addresses interconnection studies, cost allocation, co-location, and emergency curtailment
changes.after: Directs PUCT standards for new or expanded ERCOT interconnections exceeding a single-site demand threshold of 75 MW unless PUCT determines a lower threshold necessary. Other provisions have distinct scopes: Section 39.170(b) uses at least 75 MW, while Section 39.170(a) applies to certain transmission-voltage loads interconnected after 2025-12-31. Also addresses studies, cost recovery, financial commitments, qualifying co-location and conditional curtailment.
